title: Ordinary native Hom representatives determine the native derived tensor
statement: Let l be prime and Y a scheme. Put A=ProEtale.AdicSheaf l Y, with its relative module tensor [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor] and the standard derived tensor [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Let H:D(A)^op times D(A) to D(A), R:NativeHomRepresentatives(ordinaryIhomBifunctor l Y,H), and S:CoefficientClosedStructure H, in the conventions of [def-sf-native-weil-closed-models]. For every P in D(A), tensorRight for S at P is naturally isomorphic to the standard derived tensorRight at P. There is no scalar-forgetting functor, change of coefficients or derived tensor transport in this assertion, and no additional ordinary tensor model is assumed.

proof.text: Both presentations of relative tensor are coequalizers of the two balancing action maps in [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]. Their universal properties identify Mod.tensorLeft with the standard tensorRight, naturally in the fixed module. Conjugating under the two ordinary tensor-Hom adjunctions identifies Mod.ihom with the standard internal Hom, using the braiding to correct input order. Check naturality by conjugateEquiv_comp.

Apply the ordinary internal-Hom isomorphism in each pair of degrees and take products. Naturality in both variables identifies the row-sign differentials. This yields a natural isomorphism of the ordinary product-total Hom with CochainComplex.internalHom. On K-injective targets the canonical comparison with the standard derived internal Hom is an isomorphism by its K-injective computation [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom].

The model and naturality fields of R from [def-sf-native-weil-closed-models] identify H with this canonical derived internal Hom on K-injective complexes. The functor from K-injective complexes to D(A) is a localization, so fully faithful whiskering lifts the natural isomorphism to all derived targets. For each source, S.adjunction and the canonical derived tensor-Hom adjunction now have the same right adjoint. Apply Mathlib Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq; transport the chosen complex preimage to P and use the canonical braiding to obtain tensorRight.

mathlib_searches.query: An exact monoidal equivalence induces a monoidal equivalence of unbounded derived categories preserving the derived tensor product
mathlib_searches.results: Eight generic monoidal and derived-category hits. The local source library already has mapDerivedCategoryTensorComparison, usable once the ordinary comparison and native tensor identification are supplied.

Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Adjunction.Unique supplies Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq, used to compare tensors after identifying their right adjoints. It does not identify the native product-Hom complex or scalar-forgetting tensor.

mathlib_searches.query: Two left adjoints of naturally isomorphic right adjoints are naturally isomorphic
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits, including Adjunction.natIsoOfRightAdjointNatIso and Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq. The latter finishes the proof after the explicit Hom-complex and localization comparison.

theorem nativeOrdinary_tensorRight_iso (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (Y : Scheme.{u})
    (H : (DerivedCategory (ProEtale.AdicSheaf l Y))ᵒᵖ ×
      DerivedCategory (ProEtale.AdicSheaf l Y) ⥤
        DerivedCategory (ProEtale.AdicSheaf l Y))
    (R : NativeHomRepresentatives (ordinaryIhomBifunctor l Y) H)
    (S : CoefficientClosedStructure H) (P : DerivedCategory (ProEtale.AdicSheaf l Y)) :
    Nonempty (@MonoidalCategory.tensorRight _ _ S.monoidal P ≅
      MonoidalCategory.tensorRight P)
